title: When Paul Was Parted from His Friends
description: When Paul Was Parted from His Friends in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 28, “Paul's farewell charge. Acts 20:26,27”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When Paul was par-ted from his friends It was a weep-ing day; But Je-sus made them all a-mends, And wiped their tears a-way.

lines: When Paul was parted from his friends
But Jesus made them all amends,
Ere long they met again, with joy,
Thus all the preachers of his grace
But they who heard the word in vain,
Will tremble, when they meet again
On your own heads your blood will fall
The preachers, who have told you all,
Yet, Lord, to save themselves alone,
Oh bear their prayer, thy message own,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
